display.description:
CPU demand as a percentage of configured virtual CPUs. High use can be productive work; CPU waiting time provides the contention context.

Measurement details:
CPU demand relative to configured VM topology, not Kubernetes CPU request.
display.name: CPU used by each VM

spec.query: 100 * (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_cpu_usage_seconds_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]))) / ((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",source="domain",unit="cores"}) * max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",source="domain",unit="sockets"}) * max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",source="domain",unit="threads"})) > 0)

display.description:
Up to five running VMs with the most CPU scheduling wait at the end of the selected period. Values average the previous 5 minutes. A sustained increase means virtual CPUs are waiting for processing time on the host.

Measurement details:
Mean run-queue delay across vCPUs, then worst selected VM. A scheduling-pressure analogue to CPU Ready; not VMware-identical accounting. No factor of 1000: KubeVirt exports seconds.

Long names are abbreviated in this panel. Open Full names and values for complete resource labels and values. The query retains the full identity; an abbreviated name alone is not a unique identifier.

display.description:
Major page faults per second inside each VM. These reads can slow an application; compare with swap and available memory.

Measurement details:
Rate of major page faults; investigate together with swap activity and guest memory headroom.
display.name: Memory pages fetched from disk (pages/s)

display.description: Which VMs are busiest, and what could be slowing them down?
display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **Which VMs are busiest, and what could be slowing them down?** Each Top 5 selects its own VMs at the end of the selected period. Read the VM name beside its value, then select a VM to investigate its trend. High CPU use alone does not prove a problem; compare waiting time, memory pressure and disk response. **No data is not the same as zero.** Select a cluster before narrowing the next filters. **None** selects nothing; **Everything** selects all available values. After changing a cluster, reset the following filters to Everything. Full names and values opens the complete resource list.

display.description:
Time virtual CPUs spend blocked on input/output. Compare with disk response time; it is different from waiting for a turn on the CPU.

Measurement details:
Time blocked on I/O, distinct from runnable CPU scheduler delay.
display.name: Time VMs spend waiting for disk I/O

display.description:
Guest memory use after allowing for reclaimable memory. A rising value together with swap or page reads can indicate memory pressure.

Measurement details:
Guest MemAvailable-based use; different from QEMU RSS and host RAM.
display.name: Memory used inside each VM

display.description:
Up to five running VMs with the highest guest memory-use percentage at the end of the selected period. Reclaimable memory is excluded. Compare with swap activity and page reads before adding RAM.

Measurement details:
100 × (available - usable) / available. Usable corresponds to guest MemAvailable; reclaimable cache is not counted as used. Missing statistics remain empty.

Long names are abbreviated in this panel. Open Full names and values for complete resource labels and values. The query retains the full identity; an abbreviated name alone is not a unique identifier.

display.description:
Average milliseconds per completed disk read. Lower is faster. Idle disks have no measured average and remain empty.

Measurement details:
Mean seconds spent on I/O divided by completed I/Os, converted to milliseconds. One series per VM disk. Idle disks have no mean latency and remain empty.
display.name: Time to read from a VM disk (ms)

display.description:
Average percentage of time each VM's virtual CPUs wait to be scheduled. Look for increases that coincide with a slowdown.

Measurement details:
Average per-vCPU scheduling delay over 5 minutes, deduplicated by VM and vCPU ID.
display.name: Time VMs spend waiting for CPU

display.description:
Estimated bytes per second moved into or out of swap. Repeated activity can indicate insufficient guest memory; a guest reset can distort the estimate.

Measurement details:
KubeVirt exposes cumulative swap traffic as gauges. Positive 5-minute delta / 300 estimates traffic; a guest reset may invalidate this window. Not a counter rate.
display.name: VM swap traffic (bytes/s)

display.description:
Average milliseconds per completed disk write. Compare a rise with I/O wait and Longhorn storage latency.

Measurement details:
Mean seconds spent on I/O divided by completed I/Os, converted to milliseconds. One series per VM disk. Idle disks have no mean latency and remain empty.
display.name: Time to write to a VM disk (ms)
